subject: social
name: Social Studies
title: Kindergarten Social Studies: Community, Rules & American Symbols
overview: Kindergarten Social Studies introduces young scholars to civic responsibilities, geographic mapping, economic needs versus wants, and the historic stories that shape our shared community.
competencies: Explain the necessity of rules, laws, and collaborative citizenship in democratic communities.
Read and create simple maps to locate geographic features, cities, and landmarks.
Differentiate between producers, consumers, goods, and services in basic market exchanges.
Analyze primary artifacts and historical traditions celebrating American cultural diversity.

modules.title: Rules, Roles & Good Citizenship
modules.description: Understanding why communities have rules, the importance of honesty and fairness, and roles of leaders.

topics.title: Why We Have Rules
topics.description: Explaining how rules keep us safe and promote fairness in school and society.

topics.title: Responsibilities of Good Citizens
topics.description: Demonstrating respect, active listening, honesty, and collaborative teamwork.

modules.title: Geography: Maps, Globes & Neighborhoods
modules.description: Using simple maps to locate places, identifying basic land and water features on globes.

topics.title: Maps and Directions
topics.description: Using map symbols, cardinal directions, and simple floor plans to locate items.

topics.title: Land, Water & Community Places
topics.description: Distinguishing between continents, oceans, rivers, mountains, and towns.

modules.title: American Symbols, Holidays & Traditions
modules.description: Exploring patriotic symbols of the United States and national holidays honoring historic leaders.

topics.title: National Symbols & Songs
topics.description: Recognizing the American Flag, Bald Eagle, Statue of Liberty, and Liberty Bell.

topics.title: Holidays & Cultural Celebrations
topics.description: Understanding Thanksgiving, Presidents Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, and Memorial Day.
